riskTone.label: NEUTRAL
riskTone.rationale: FTSE 100 flat with mixed sector moves; US-Iran tension adds mild risk-off, offset by energy gains; no strong directional signal.

briefing.briefing: Sterling (GBPUSD) is up +0.19% today, which — because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions — is a mild headwind for the FTSE 100; a stronger pound makes the index's overseas dollar-earners (like Shell, Unilever, AstraZeneca) worth less when translated back into sterling, so this is a small drag on the index. That said, the GBP impact is rated NEUTRAL overall, so it is not the dominant force today. The real story in the regime is a tug-of-war: Energy (Shell, BP) is strongly bullish with Brent crude up a striking +4.52% — almost certainly linked to the US-Iran tensions flagged in a Reuters headline from roughly 19 hours ago — and Miners (Rio, Glencore, Anglo) are also bullish with copper up +1.63%, suggesting markets still see reasonable global growth. However, those gains are being offset by a slightly soggy European tape (DAX -0.34%, EuroStoxx -0.16%), a small gap-down open of roughly -39 points this morning, and positioning data showing that big speculative traders are heavily 'crowded short' on GBP, which the model flags as a bearish read-through for FTSE. Gilt yields (the interest rate the UK government pays to borrow money) are marginally lower today — down 2 basis points on the 10-year — and long-end stress is absent, so there is no fiscal alarm signal. The most important catalyst still ahead is US CPI (inflation data) at 13:30 BST today — a HIGH-impact release that could jolt the dollar, gilts, and the whole index in either direction. Build-up caution: UK GDP data arrives Wednesday at 07:00 BST, just before London cash open, and could set the tone for the second half of the week. Directional bias is very slightly bullish (score +1) purely because energy and miners — two of the heaviest index sectors — are providing genuine commodity-driven support, but conviction is LOW because the ORB already broke downward this morning and 69% of the average daily range (128 points) has already been consumed, leaving only about 40 points of typical range remaining — meaning the index is statistically closer to its daily 'ceiling' of movement than its floor. Key levels to watch: overnight high 10499.9 and prior-day high 10526.3 as resistance above; ORB low 10447.4 and overnight low 10414.8 as support below; the current price of 10451.35 is sitting just above the ORB low after the downside break. Today's ORB break was to the downside, but with energy surging and CPI looming at 13:30 BST, this looks more like a fakeout or chop day than a clean trend — the macro picture is too mixed and the event risk too close to press a directional ORB trade with confidence; standing aside or using very tight risk management until after 13:30 is the prudent call. Confidence: 4/10 — a hotter-than-expected US CPI print could slam risk assets and confirm the downside ORB break, while a softer print could reverse it entirely and push energy-led gains to the fore. Screenshot this: the ORB broke down but energy is screaming higher — wait for 13:30 CPI before trusting any direction.
